name: Nokia 3310
blurb: Nokia's near-indestructible 2000 phone with swappable covers and Snake II
title: Nokia 3310: Release Date, Snake II and the 2017 Remake
description: The Nokia 3310 was a GSM phone announced in September 2000, known for toughness, swappable covers and Snake II. It sold 126 million and was remade in 2017.
answer: The Nokia 3310 was a compact GSM mobile phone announced on 1 September 2000, with a small monochrome screen, swappable covers and the game Snake II built in. It became famous for being almost impossible to break and sold about 126 million units before production ended in December 2005. In 2017 HMD Global, which licensed the Nokia phone brand, launched a modern colour-screen remake.

body: The 3310 was a chunky candybar phone with an 84×48-pixel monochrome display and a handful of buttons. It did calls and texts, could join several SMS into one long message of up to 459 characters, and had a Chat feature that worked a bit like instant messaging over SMS, plus a calculator, stopwatch and reminders.
Its Xpress-on covers clipped off and on, so a new colour made it feel like a new phone. It shipped with more than 35 ringtones and user profiles.

The original Snake was written in 1997 by Nokia engineer Taneli Armanto for the monochrome Nokia 6110. The 3310 had the sequel, Snake II, which added mazes and let the snake wrap around the screen edges instead of dying.
Four games came built in: Snake II, the side-scrolling shooter Space Impact, the memory game Pairs II, and Bantumi, a version of the mancala board game.

head: Year
What happened
rows: 1 September: Nokia announces the 3310, replacing the 3210
December: production ends after about 126 million units
Finland includes the 3310, nicknamed "The Unbreakable", among its national emojis
February: HMD Global unveils the new 3310 at Mobile World Congress for €49

body: The original is long discontinued and now a second-hand and collector item. The 2017 remake has a colour screen, a design that nods to the original and a redesigned colour version of Snake; a 3G version followed. HMD still has a Nokia 3310 product page. The remake shares the name and shape, not the hardware.

faq.a: It was genuinely tough, and the "indestructible" reputation became a long-running internet joke; Finland even nicknamed its emoji "The Unbreakable".
About 126 million units between 2000 and the end of production in 2005.
The Nokia 6110, in 1997. The 3310 had the sequel, Snake II.
